title: COMP 3721 · Week 6
subtitle: Bandwidth utilization (FDM, WDM, TDM) and the data-link layer (services, MAC addresses, ARP), preparing for Quiz 6
description: Lecture 06a: bandwidth utilization, multiplexing one link into n channels, FDM with carriers and guard bands and the 20 to 32 kHz example, WDM on fibre, synchronous TDM with units, slots and frames, the 1 Mbps × 4 example, empty slots, multilevel multiplexing, multiple-slot allocation, pulse stuffing and framing bits, with both slide examples worked. Lecture 06b: node-to-node communication, framing and the frame, the four services and two sublayers, why link-layer addresses exist and change at every hop, 48-bit MAC addresses, the layer-2 switch, ARP's broadcast request and unicast reply with the packet format, and Alice's datagram to Bob through R1 and R2 frame by frame. A live widget for each idea, Mock Quiz 6 and the Week 6 study note.
intro:
:::quiz Quiz 6 scope
Quiz 5 covers Lectures 05a and 05b, so Quiz 6 is expected to cover Lectures 06a and 06b, all of it in this module. The calculations are FDM link bandwidth with guard bands (n channels, n − 1 guard bands) and synchronous TDM rates (frame rate = input unit rate, link bit rate = n × input rate, frame duration, bit duration). Write Hz for a bandwidth, bps for a bit rate, frames/s for a frame rate and seconds for a duration. The data-link half is definitions and the order of the addresses in a frame. One A4 or letter page of notes, single-sided and preferably hand-written, is allowed; the last lesson is the Week 6 block of that page.
:::

multiple of others → multilevel or multiple-slot; not a multiple → pulse stuffing
IP source-destination, link-layer destination-source; which L changes at each hop
request broadcast, reply unicast; operation 1 and 2; empty destination hardware address
write the three frames yourself before stepping the widget
hand-write the Week 6 block of your A4 page from this draft
